notes: The kernel family: complete-set split and merge, finite resolution, exact and refused redemption, transfer conservation, the phase gate, and the two landed check-order facts R1 and R8.

provenance.rationale: The proposal's own worked example, ported as the first real vector. Smallest trace exercising complete-set split, finite resolution, and an exact integral redemption whose maximum-liability requirement drops from 11 to 1. total_supply[0] stays at 11 after redemption because outcome 0 carries weight 0 under the resolved vector; tidying it to 0 would encode a supply leak.

vectors.title: complete split, finite resolution, exact one-hot redemption

provenance.rationale: merge is the exact inverse of split on the merged quantity: collateral and every outcome supply fall by exactly the merged amount, and the residual maximum-liability requirement equals the residual collateral. Derived by reading split/merge and required_for_vector, with the crate's own test as the reference reading.

vectors.title: split then partial merge conserves collateral and every outcome supply

provenance.rationale: transfer_internal takes &self, so supply and collateral neutrality is structural rather than checked. The vector pins the whole market state across two transfers so a future signature change to &mut self could not pass silently.

vectors.title: a transfer relabels a holder without touching supply or collateral

provenance.rationale: The single fault is the sender's balance: the quantity is nonzero, the outcome is in range, the market is Active, and the receiver cannot overflow. The final_state is the whole state after the refusal, which is what makes post_state_on_error "unchanged" a checked claim rather than a comment.

vectors.title: a transfer above the holder's balance is refused and moves nothing

provenance.rationale: The P1-A fixture: one payout vector with weights [1, 1] over denominator 2. One atom of each outcome is solvent (collateral 1) but exit-dead through every single-outcome path, because 1 * 1 is not divisible by 2. sum_i q * w_i = q * D makes the complete set exact unconditionally, so redeem_complete_set pays exactly 1 and closes the market. Expected values derived by reading redeem and redeem_complete_set, not by running a generator.

vectors.title: P1-A: every single-outcome redemption remainders forever, the complete set is exact

provenance.rationale: Three sets are not held after one atom of outcome 0 leaves, so the short leg is a balance fault, not a remainder fault. The rescue of POLICY_ANALYSIS_LOTS_FEES.md 1.5 is for balanced positions only: the recipient of the single atom is still permanently exit-dead, and step 6 pins that.

vectors.title: an unbalanced fractional holding is refused as a balance fault and stays exit-dead

provenance.rationale: The phase gate precedes the balance and quantity gates on all three redemption paths, so the reported fact is the phase and not the (also true) absence of a resolved payout vector.

vectors.title: redemption before resolution is refused on every redemption path

provenance.rationale: require_active returns AlreadyResolved, never NotActive: R6 records that kernel::Error::NotActive is declared and never constructed anywhere in the tree, so this vector deliberately expects 3002 and code 3001 stays vector-less on this surface.

vectors.title: every Active-only transition is refused once the market is Resolved

comparison.precedence_note: merge validates shape, checks invariants, requires Active, refuses zero quantity, then tests collateral < quantity, and only then tests the per-outcome balances. Because weights sum to the denominator, any state passing the balance tests already holds collateral >= quantity, so 5002 is observable from merge only through this ordering.

provenance.rationale: An empty market fails both the collateral test and the per-outcome balance tests. Which code is observable is decided purely by the documented check order, so this vector pins that order as landed behaviour. Reordering the two checks would make code 5002 unreachable from merge and relabel a whole family of inputs; that is a reviewable decision, not a refactor.

vectors.title: R8: merge's collateral test precedes its balance tests, and the order is observable

provenance.rationale: Position::validate_outcome raises InvalidPayoutIndex for an out-of-range *outcome*, while PayoutSet::get raises the same variant for an out-of-range *payout vector*. The vector names the exact fact (2062) and the executor answers with the coarse 2060, which is admitted only because kernel::Error::InvalidPayoutIndex declares coarsens [2061, 2062]. If R1 option (a) is taken and the variant is split, this vector becomes an exact match with no edit.

vectors.title: R1: an out-of-range outcome index is reported through the coarse payout-index variant
